builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Neural Dimensional Analysis: Foundations of Dimensionless and Scale-Consistent Computation
summary: The method replaces standard scale-control machinery (layer normalization, residual scaling, attention temperature, loss weighting) with a dimensional-consistency framework implemented as the Gauge-Canonical Transformer with normalized coordinates and orthogonalized residual additions. The cost is that benefits accrue only when training a model from scratch under this architecture, plus implementation complexity in reworking residual streams, attention inputs, and multi-loss objectives. It can fail to transfer if adopted piecemeal onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and its quantization-robustness and stability claims are demonstrated only up to 1B parameters on the authors' training setup.
rationale: The reader cannot pretrain foundation models, so the core contribution is not directly adoptable, but the quantization-robustness and training-stability findings warrant monitoring for integration into future open-weight checkpoints.
technique: Neural Dimensional Analysis and Gauge-Canonical Transformer

claims.statement: The method replaces standard scale-control machinery (layer normalization, residual scaling, attention temperature, loss weighting) with a dimensional-consistency framework implemented as the Gauge-Canonical Transformer with normalized coordinates and orthogonalized residual additions. The cost is that benefits accrue only when training a model from scratch under this architecture, plus implementation complexity in reworking residual streams, attention inputs, and multi-loss objectives. It can fail to transfer if adopted piecemeal onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and its quantization-robustness and stability claims are demonstrated only up to 1B parameters on the authors' training setup.

GCT remains stable across a sixteenfold learning-rate range and outperforms Pre-LN, LLaMA-style, and QK-Norm baselines in 124M validation loss; at 1B parameters, calibrated per-tensor int8 quantization raises GCT validation loss by only 0.009 nats versus up to 5.51 nats for baselines.
